content.value_statement: Autonomous agents can fail through compounding errors, runaway costs, weak guardrails, and poor observability. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code patterns for safer agent loops, approvals, checkpointing, and reliability checks.
actual_capabilities: Explains ReAct, Plan-Execute, and reflection loop patterns for agent design.
Shows LangGraph checkpointing, interrupts, and time-travel debugging patterns.
Defines guardrails for cost limits, allowed actions, approvals, rollback, and least privilege.
Documents failure modes such as context growth, fabricated data, dangerous actions, and integration failures.
Provides validation checks for step limits, timeouts, structured output, checkpointing, and rollback.
limitations: Does not provide a complete runnable agent application.
Requires environment-specific testing before production use.
Uses illustrative code snippets that may need framework updates.
Does not replace security review for agents with write access or external integrations.

use_cases.title: Design a Production Agent Loop
use_cases.description: Plan a constrained agent using ReAct, Plan-Execute, reflection, step limits, and human approval gates.

use_cases.title: Review Reliability Controls
use_cases.description: Check an agent design for cost limits, checkpointing, retries, observability, and rollback behavior.

use_cases.title: Define Agent Safety Requirements
use_cases.description: Turn product goals into clear boundaries for permissions, evidence, validation, and escalation.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Agent Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new agent workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me decide whether ReAct, Plan-Execute, or reflection fits this task: [describe task]. Include risks and required guardrails.

prompt_templates.title: Add Basic Guardrails
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent plan for missing step limits, timeouts, cost controls, approval gates, and rollback points: [paste plan].

prompt_templates.title: Plan Durable Execution
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a durable execution approach for this long-running agent: [describe workflow]. Include checkpointing, thread IDs, recovery, and observability.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Agent Before Launch
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this autonomous agent design for production risk: [paste design]. Prioritize dangerous actions, fabricated data, integration failure, and context growth.

output_examples.input: A team wants an agent to process support refunds with minimal human review.
output_examples.output: The response recommends limiting autonomous steps, separating read and write permissions, requiring approval for refunds, logging every action, and adding rollback plans.

output_examples.input: A developer asks why a long-running research agent becomes slow and expensive.
output_examples.output: The response explains context growth, proposes token budgets, summarizes old context, tracks costs, and stops work near the budget limit.

output_examples.input: A product manager asks how to launch an agent safely.
output_examples.output: The response provides a staged rollout plan with test coverage, observability, approval gates, and metrics for reliability and cost.

best_practices: Set maximum steps, timeouts, and cost limits before adding more tools.
Require human approval for write, payment, email, deletion, or production changes.
Log decisions, tool calls, checkpoints, and rollback actions for every agent run.
anti_patterns: Giving a general agent broad permissions without a defined task boundary.
Running long tasks without checkpointing, thread IDs, or recovery behavior.
Acting on agent outputs without validation, evidence, or structured schemas.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design reliable autonomous agents with clear loops, guardrails, checkpointing, and human review.

faq.question: Does it create a full agent application?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture patterns, examples, and review checks for your implementation.

faq.question: Which agent patterns are covered?
faq.answer: It covers ReAct, Plan-Execute, reflection, guardrailed autonomy, durable execution, and human-in-the-loop interrupts.

faq.question: Can it help with LangGraph designs?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes LangGraph examples for checkpointing, interrupts, state graphs, and debugging.

faq.question: How does it reduce production risk?
faq.answer: It emphasizes limits, least privilege, validation, evidence, observability, rollback, and staged deployment.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for engineering, platform, or product work on agents that plan, call tools, or run multiple steps.
